latestPosts.caption:
Linkin Park wasn’t just a band — they were a *gateway*.
The first time those distorted synths slammed into rap verses and raw emotion, something rewired in my brain.

They made techno feel angry, rap feel vulnerable, and rock feel futuristic.
Before playlists, before algorithms — LP taught a whole generation how genres could *collide* and still make sense.

For millennials, this wasn’t background music.
This was headphones on, volume maxed, feeling-seen-at-2AM music.
From **Hybrid Theory** to **Meteora**, they walked so today’s electronic, rap, and alt scenes could run.

If you ever screamed the chorus, nodded through the verses, or got pulled into techno and rap because of them — you know.
Linkin Park forever shaped the sound of our chaos. 🖤❤️🥰

#LinkinPark #MillennialAnthem #HybridTheory #Meteora #TechnoRoots RapRock ForeverLP

latestPosts.caption:
Secret’s out! 🤭🤰🏻Can you believe it????

I spent my entire first trimester on the Mongol Rally 🤣 And I honestly wouldn’t change it. I was 8 weeks along when we arrived in Tbilisi, Georgia, and so we paid $30 to get an ultrasound. They allowed ALL 9 OF US to be in the room together for the most shocking, magical, emotional, beautiful experience of my life! Getting to see an actual baby with a beating heart inside of me for the first time - the little thing that had been making me nauseas, vomit, hormonal, bloated, excited, and terrified all at the same time - was actually REAL. I am in love with this feeling and don’t think I can ever get over it. And getting to share that experience with a room full of people I love so much was a dream I didn’t even know I had. 

Just WOW! Thank you to everyone who watched our announcement video - I can FEEL all of your love and joy to my core! Nate and I are so grateful. This week has been indescribable. Thank you thank you thank you 🥹💛

Nate made a goal in 2026 to run 100 miles on all 7 continents, and South America was #4!! 🙌🏼 🇦🇷

He finished 87th out of 600, and went harder and faster than ever before. He pushed himself to a find new limit he didn’t know he had. I could see it and feel it every time I saw him along the way. As always I’m in awe of him ❤️

And how does he look the same after running up and down mountains for 31 hours?? 😍

Now to hobble him to bed with some pizza and pain relievers 😅 Thank you for all the love and support the last few days! Love ya!

latestPosts.caption:
🇨🇦 Canada ka ek interesting FOOD LAW! 😳

Did you know that packaged foods sold in Canada are legally required to display prominent warnings if they contain high levels of certain nutrients?
⚠️ HIGH IN SUGARS
⚠️ HIGH IN SATURATED FAT
⚠️ HIGH IN SODIUM
Introduced in 2022 and mandatory for qualifying products since January 2026, this rule makes it easier for consumers to identify certain nutritional concerns without searching through the fine print.
And yes, this applies to Indian food brands selling in Canada too! 🇮🇳
From biscuits and namkeen to pickles and instant noodles, you might be surprised by what these labels reveal! 👀
Do you think these warnings actually influence what people buy? Or do we simply ignore them? 🤔

Linkin Park wasn’t just a band — they were a *gateway*.
The first time those distorted synths slammed into rap verses and raw emotion, something rewired in my brain.

They made techno feel angry, rap feel vulnerable, and rock feel futuristic.
Before playlists, before algorithms — LP taught a whole generation how genres could *collide* and still make sense.

For millennials, this wasn’t background music.
This was headphones on, volume maxed, feeling-seen-at-2AM music.
From **Hybrid Theory** to **Meteora**, they walked so today’s electronic, rap, and alt scenes could run.

If you ever screamed the chorus, nodded through the verses, or got pulled into techno and rap because of them — you know.
Linkin Park forever shaped the sound of our chaos. 🖤❤️🥰

Thayambaka - Thayambaka is a ritual temple art that is often performed at annual festivals, but it can also be performed outside of temples at proscenium stages, open fields, or pageantry grounds. 
The structure of a thayambaka recital is thought to have developed from a combination of the classical Carnatic music of Tamil Nadu and the percussion tradition of central Kerala. 
The main instrument in a thayambaka is the chenda, a drum made from the soft wood of the jackfruit tree. The chenda is often used to accompany other forms of dance and rituals in Kerala, such as Kathakali, Koodiyattam, and Kannyar Kali.
